inputs.base_revenue_note: FY2025 revenue from sales (ex excise), USD m. FY2025 was a near-mid-cycle year (Brent $69/b, realized gas $5.72/MBtu, ERM $7.1/b) and is deliberately used as the compounding base instead of FY2026, which carries the Middle East conflict windfall (H1 2026 Brent $92/b, ERM ~$33/b in Q3). The windfall is modelled as a one-year Year-1 spike that unwinds in Years 2-3, not as the base.
inputs.share_count_basis: Shares issued 2,281,656,714 less 57,468,046 treasury shares at June 30, 2026 (H1 2026 report, statement of changes in equity p.46 and Note 4). Includes the 100,985,040 shares issued in H1 2026 as acquisition currency for 50% of EPH's European flexible-power portfolio (genuine non-SBC issuance, already in the count). Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, so performance-share dilution is charged once there. Q3 2026 buybacks ($1.5bn, ~16m shares) post-date the balance sheet and are not netted, to keep the count on the same date as net debt.
inputs.net_debt_note: Company-defined net debt $19,710m at June 30, 2026 (H1 2026 report s.1.10.5: current borrowings 11,229 + other current financial liabilities 209 + HFS net financial assets 114 + non-current financial debt 41,157 - current financial assets 3,720 - non-current financial assets 1,601 - cash 27,678) PLUS lease liabilities $8,904m (treatment A, leases as debt) = $28,614m. total_debt = 11,229 + 209 + 41,157 + 8,904 = 61,499; cash = 27,678 + 3,720 + 1,601 - 114 = 32,885. Perpetual subordinated notes (IFRS equity) and NCI are deducted separately in equity_bridge.
inputs.interest_income_note: FY2025 interest income $1,115m is NOT stripped: TotalEnergies is a net-debt company (gearing 13.1%), so the cash earning it is already netted against borrowings in the bridge. Stripping it would charge the cash twice in the other direction.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 Annual Report, statement of changes in equity, 'Share-based payments' $585m (FY2024 $556m, FY2023 $291m); H1 2026 $372m. French performance-share plans; no cash taxes on net-share settlement (EquityAwardTaxes 0 across history).
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 share buybacks $7,714m (cash flow statement); H1 2026 $2,286m; Q3 2026 $1.5bn and Q4 2026 $2.5bn authorized. The flat count is being funded many times over by actual repurchases.
inputs.fx_note: fx_rate is EUR per USD (model USD -> quote EUR): 1 / EURUSD 1.1213 (Yahoo EURUSD=X, 2026-10-25T22:40Z). Parity check against the NYSE ADR (TTE, 1 ADR = 1 ordinary share): Paris close EUR 83.45 x 1.1213 = USD 93.57 vs ADR close USD 92.78 on 2026-10-23, a 0.85% gap explained by the ADR closing 4.5 hours after Paris. Confirms direction, the 1:1 ADR ratio and the quote basis. Reporting currency has been USD since FY2012; all flows, net debt and the bridge are USD; per-share values are converted to EUR at this single rate. refresh_price.py does not refresh fx_rate: re-derive it when the price is refreshed.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in USD, the currency of the flows. Rf 4.2% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, beta 0.95 (integrated majors) -> cost of equity 9.0%. Pre-tax cost of debt 5.0%, after-tax ~3.75% at a ~25% blended statutory rate. Weights from market values: equity ~$208bn (2,224m x EUR 83.45 x 1.1213), debt-like claims ~$41bn (net debt 19.7 + leases 8.9 + hybrids 12.7) -> D/(D+E) ~16%. WACC = 0.84 x 9.0 + 0.16 x 3.75 = 8.2%, rounded to 8.0%. The same 8.0% is used in every scenario: commodity, geopolitical and transition risk are charged ONCE, in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked on the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: A (leases as debt). Lease liabilities $8,904m (June 30, 2026) sit in net_debt; lease principal is NOT deducted from the flows. Ongoing lease-asset renewal (~$1.8bn/yr: on-balance-sheet lease payments of $2,616m in 2026 falling to ~$1.3bn by 2029, FY2025 AR Note 7; average ~1.0% of revenue) is charged through the capex line, which is set at net investments guidance ($14-16bn/yr) plus ~1.0pp for lease renewal. D&A includes right-of-use depreciation, consistent with treatment A. Short-term/exempted lease contracts (~$0.9bn/yr) are already inside opex/EBITDA.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are consolidated (adjusted EBITDA includes 100% of subsidiaries), so non-controlling interests are deducted once in the bridge at book ($2,545m at June 30, 2026). NCI share of net income is small ($159m of $11,407m in H1 2026), so book is an adequate proxy.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component build, scenario-weighted, with the cyclical adaptations (dcf-methods owner-fcf-adaptations.md: currency a1/a2, leases b, NCI c, risk-once f). TotalEnergies is an integrated oil & gas and power producer: an operating company whose value is a stream of free cash flow, so the owner-FCF route applies; no part of it is a bank, REIT or holdco. MID-CYCLE NORMALISATION: FY2025 (Brent $69) is the revenue base. Year 1 (FY2026) carries the conflict windfall (+17% revenue, 24% EBITDA margin vs H1 2026 actual 24.1%); Years 2-3 unwind it toward a $70 Brent / $10 TTF / $7 ERM mid-cycle (base), the company's own $60 planning deck (bear), or a sustained $85 premium (bull). From Year 4 revenue grows only with guided volumes (~3%/yr hydrocarbons to 2030, Integrated Power to 100-120 TWh) at flat nominal prices. Peak FY2026 FCF is NOT extrapolated. EQUITY BRIDGE deducts perpetual subordinated notes ($12,745m: $10,994m at Dec 31 2025 per FY2025 AR Note 9 + $1,751m net issuance in H1 2026) because they are debt-like claims senior to common equity whose coupons ($320m in FY2025) never pass through the P&L or the FCF, and NCI ($2,545m). Russia: the 19.4% Novatek stake (no longer equity-accounted, written down ~$14.8bn in 2022) and 20% Yamal LNG ($5.8bn carrying value) are left at zero incremental value in the bridge; Yamal cash flows that do arrive are inside the consolidated flows. TERMINAL CAP: 13x FCF base (12x bear, 15x bull) per the method's 12-15x guidance for cyclicals; Gordon at 8%/2% would be 17x, so the cap binds in every scenario and is recorded as such. The horizon is 10 years so the Year-1 windfall and its unwind are explicit rather than capitalised.

equity_bridge.item: Perpetual subordinated notes (hybrids in IFRS equity, debt-like)
equity_bridge.note: $10,994m at Dec 31, 2025 (FY2025 AR Note 9) + $1,751m net issuance H1 2026 (statement of changes in equity). Coupons $320m/yr paid out of equity, not in the flows.
H1 2026 report, June 30, 2026 balance sheet. Flows are consolidated; NCI deducted once here.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: management volume guidance (hydrocarbon production ~+3%/yr to 2030; electricity 100-120 TWh by 2030) at flat nominal prices, applied from Year 4; Years 1-3 are a price-cycle path, not a growth rate
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 2.1% vs revenue 5yr CAGR 8.8% and owner-FCF 5yr CAGR 20.6%: the divergence is entirely base-effect from the FY2020 trough (Brent $42, net loss -$7.2bn). 3yr CAGRs from the FY2022 peak (Brent $101) are deeply negative. Neither window is a growth signal for a commodity producer; historical CAGRs are reported for completeness and NOT used to set the growth path.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF = reported FCF - SBC (no interest-income strip: net-debt company). FY2020 owner FCF 3,851 -> FY2025 9,805 (5yr +20.6%); FY2022 31,448 -> FY2025 9,805 (3yr -32.2%). SBC grew from $188m (FY2020) to $585m (FY2025), 0.16% -> 0.32% of revenue; owner-FCF CAGRs sit ~0.2pp below reported in both windows, immaterial. EPS 5yr CAGR undefined (FY2020 EPS -2.90). Equity CAGR is suppressed by $25bn+ of annual dividends and buybacks (55% of CFFO in FY2025).

base.growth_note: Y1 FY2026 ~$213bn: H1 actual $106.6bn, H2 similar on Brent ~$85 and ERM >$30. Y2 FY2027 Brent eases to ~$75, ERM to ~$12. Y3 FY2028 Brent $70 / TTF $10 / ERM $7 mid-cycle with +3% volumes. Y4-Y6 +2.5% (guided ~3% hydrocarbon volume growth less Europe downstream volume decline, plus power). Y7-Y10 +2.0% as LNG growth plateaus post-2030.
base.ebitda_note: Adjusted EBITDA / revenue: FY2021 22.9%, FY2022 27.2%, FY2023 22.9%, FY2024 22.1%, FY2025 22.2%, H1 2026 24.1%. Mid-cycle set at 22.0%, 0.2pp below FY2025, because adjusted EBITDA includes non-cash equity-affiliate income above the dividends actually received (~$1bn/yr gap between EBITDA-less-tax and unlevered CFFO).
base.da_note: D&A ~$14bn/yr (FY2025 $13,847m, H1 2026 $7,246m) held roughly flat in dollars: 6.6% on the windfall revenue, 7.4% at mid-cycle.
base.capex_note: Net investments guided ~$15bn for FY2026 and $14-16bn/yr 2026-2030, plus ~$1.8bn/yr lease-asset renewal under lease treatment A => ~$16.6-16.8bn/yr: 7.8% of $213bn, 8.5% of $196bn, 8.8% of $190bn. Reported FY2025 capex $16,953m included $3.9bn of acquisitions.
base.tax_note: Cash tax paid / (EBITDA - SBC - D&A): FY2023 35.3%, FY2024 35.8%, FY2025 36.8%; company effective tax rate 37.5-39.8%. High-price years skew to upstream, taxed at 50%+, hence 38% in Y1.
base.wc_note: Receivables + inventories exceed payables for a producer-refiner; working capital absorbs ~3% of any revenue increase and releases it when revenue falls. The Y1 windfall therefore consumes ~$0.9bn and Y2-Y3 release ~$0.7bn.
base.narrative: Mid-cycle normalisation: the 2026 conflict windfall is collected once, prices revert to ~$70 Brent by 2028, and value accrues from guided volume growth, the $12.5bn 2026-30 cost programme and a 13x terminal FCF multiple.

bull.narrative: Structurally higher deck: Brent holds ~$85 through 2028 on a prolonged Hormuz disruption and OPEC+ discipline; LNG grows to 60 Mt/y at premium Asian pricing; Integrated Power reaches its 12% ROACE target; the cost programme lifts mid-cycle margin to 23.5%; the market pays 15x for a lower-carbon-intensity major.

bear.narrative: The company's own $60/b planning deck becomes reality: conflict resolves, Brent falls to $60 / TTF $8 / ERM $5 by 2028, European product volumes decline, carbon costs rise toward $100/t, Middle East curtailments linger, capex is sticky at ~$16.5bn on lower revenue, and the terminal multiple compresses to 12x on transition risk.

scenario_narratives.base: Revenue spikes ~17% in FY2026 on the Middle East conflict (Brent $92 in H1, European refining margin above $30/b in Q3) and the 24% EBITDA margin seen in H1 2026, then unwinds over FY2027-28 to a $70 Brent / $10 TTF / $7 ERM mid-cycle at a 22.0% margin. From 2029 revenue grows ~2.5%/yr with guided hydrocarbon volumes (+3%/yr to 2030: Mero, Anchor/Ballymore, North Field East, Tilenga, Ratawi) and Integrated Power scaling toward 100-120 TWh, fading to 2.0%. Capex is held at the $14-16bn net-investment guidance plus lease renewal; cash tax at the 36.5% the company has actually paid. Owner FCF settles around $15bn at mid-cycle, consistent with management's path of ~$10bn FCF growth by 2030 vs 2024 at constant prices. Terminal value is the 13x cap, not Gordon.
scenario_narratives.bull: A durable price premium: the Strait of Hormuz disruption and Russian refining outages keep Brent near $85 and the ERM in the teens through 2028, LNG sales climb toward 60 Mt/y at JKM-linked pricing, and Integrated Power hits its 12% ROACE target by 2028. The $12.5bn 2026-30 cost programme lifts the mid-cycle EBITDA margin to 23.5%, capex falls to the low end of guidance as a share of a larger revenue base, and the market grants a 15x terminal FCF multiple to the major with the largest low-carbon power platform. Owner FCF runs ~$19-20bn mid-cycle.
scenario_narratives.bear: The windfall reverses: conflict resolution plus non-OPEC supply growth pushes Brent to $60 and the ERM to $5 by 2028, exactly the company's conservative planning case (CFFO ~$26bn, net investments $15bn -> FCF ~$11bn). Middle East production remains curtailed longer than management expects, European fuel demand declines, EU-ETS costs climb toward $100/t, and Russia-linked assets stay frozen. Capex is sticky in dollars against a ~$170bn revenue base (9.6%), the margin compresses to 20.5%, and the terminal multiple compresses to 12x on stranded-asset concerns. Owner FCF settles near $10-11bn, in line with the company's own $60 deck.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 30% and bull cut from 35% to 20%. The stock sits at a 52-week high (EUR 83.45 vs a 52.4-83.74 range) on earnings inflated by a geopolitical shock the company itself describes as temporary, and the bear path is not a stress case but management's own $60/b planning deck plus a normal downstream margin. The bull case needs several independent things to persist at once: a sustained Hormuz premium, LNG premium pricing AND Integrated Power reaching 12% ROACE. Base at 50% is the mid-cycle reversion that both history (FY2023-25 margins) and the company's guidance point to.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value an integrated major on mid-cycle owner FCF, not on the current price deck. FY2025 ($69 Brent) is the base; the 2026 windfall is a one-year flow explicitly collected and then unwound; terminal value is capped at 12-15x FCF because Gordon at 8%/2% implies 17x, a multiple no buyer has paid for an oil major. Hybrids and NCI are deducted as claims senior to common equity. All flows are USD and converted to EUR once at a dated, parity-checked rate.
key_risks_to_valuation: Oil and gas price path: a $10/b Brent move is ~$2.8bn/yr of CFFO (company sensitivity); the scenarios span $60-85 but a sustained move outside that band dominates every other driver
Terminal multiple judgment: the 13x cap, not Gordon, sets terminal value in every scenario (roughly half of EV); at 15x the base value rises materially, at 11x it falls
FX: EUR per-share values move one-for-one with EUR/USD; a 5% stronger euro cuts the EUR IV ~5% with no change in the USD business
Reinvestment efficiency: Integrated Power ROACE ~9.7% is near the 8% WACC, so $2-3bn/yr of the capex line creates little value if returns do not reach the 12% target
Middle East concentration (34% of production) and Russia (Novatek, Yamal LNG, Arctic LNG 2): tail events outside the three-scenario frame
Energy-transition demand and carbon pricing after 2030: the company's own $200/t CO2 stress case cuts discounted asset value ~15%
